result.summary: Both candidates rejected; no remaining defects. Candidate 1: blank replace fields with a retained draft after hide/show is the disclosed and tested retention behavior (panel text 'Replace starts blank. Entered values stay only in Project memory and are never echoed back'; test line 60 asserts blank field with retained draft after reopen). Erase runs under updating=true so it cannot corrupt the draft. Candidate 2: premise that bump() does not emit is false; bump -> bindProbe -> probes.setView(null) always reaches publish("idle") (the equality early-return applies only to non-null next), firing probes.onChange{emit()} subscribed at gateway line 50, so a render follows the draft removal and the null-draft path resets the form and renderedGeneration.

obligations.evidence: Hide erases fields via erase() under updating=true, so no draft mutation. Retained draft with blank replace field is the disclosed policy (ConnectionFieldsPanel line 102 text; Panel test line 60 asserts empty password field while the draft is retained after dispose/reopen). Save submits only the user's own earlier-entered value held in Project memory; no leak, ownership or scope violation. Candidate remedy would contradict approved retention.

Gateway lines 83/81-82: bump() calls bindProbe(), which calls probes.setView(null) when the draft is null. ConnectionDraftTests line 49-50: with next==null the early return is skipped; cancel(); identity=null; publish('idle') runs unconditionally, firing listeners. Gateway line 50 subscribes probes.onChange{emit()}. So an emit always follows the draft removal at line 94 (unless disposed, in which case live() is false anyway). Panel re-renders with null draft; fields.render form==null branch clears the form and formId; renderedGeneration updates, so the action guard is not stuck.

limitations: ConnectionDraft.clear() and the rest of ConnectionDraftTests.kt were not supplied; rejection of candidate 2 relies on the visible setView/publish code and the gateway line-50 subscription.
